messages:
marie: Ran into a surprising CI failure when rotating keys in infra templates. The new REDWOOD_API_KEY was set but the running demo still auth'd with RW_LEGACY_TOKEN. :grimacing:

oscar: Which sample uses RW_LEGACY_TOKEN?

marie: deploy-starter. Repro steps: set both envs, rotate REDWOOD_API_KEY via rw rotate-key, app continues using RW_LEGACY_TOKEN if present.

dee: That means our rotate flow isn't atomic for deployments that have legacy env names pinned. Some repos pinned older SDKs with different precedence.

marie: Minimal repro: 
```bash
export RW_LEGACY_TOKEN=old123
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=new456
./start-demo  # still uses old123
```

oscar: Short-term: update rotate-key helper in infra-templates to write all known env names (REDWOOD_API_KEY, RW_LEGACY_TOKEN, RW_PROJECT_KEY, RW_ORG_KEY) so rotation isn't partial.

infra-bot: CI job #3087 failed: https://ci.internal/3087 401 unauthorized

dee: Also add a one-line deprecation log in SDKs when a legacy env is present and link to a migration doc. That will reduce silent surprises.

marie: Can we add a SIGHUP handler in starter so containers re-init client on signal? Many deployments don't restart automatically when secrets change.

oscar: Good idea. Add an e2e in CI: run rotate-key, signal container or restart, then assert requests succeed. Catch pinned-sdk behavior early.

dee: Longer term: RFC to standardize canonical env precedence across languages (recommend REDWOOD_API_KEY first) and publish streaming rotation guidance: prefer handshake auth and require reconnect on token change; servers should fail fast on auth error.

sam: I'll open the infra-templates PR for dual-write and the sampleapp SIGHUP handler. dee  can you file the SDK deprecation + migration doc?

dee: On it. Creating issues and linking from the PR.

oscar: Thanks team. This kind of mixed-secrets state is exactly why we need the onboarding "CI secret hygiene" blurb.
